newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P posts dramatic reversal, ends down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P posts dramatic reversal, ends down.

text.p: U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended lower after an afternoon of heavy losses in what traders called a dramatic reversal from record highs.

March rallied again into uncharted territory early in the session and fell just shy of psychologically key 800.00 before coming under pressure just before T-bond futures closed. After the T-bond close, losses began to mount and technical sales and panic selling slammed the market, traders said.
"It really fell out of bed," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "It was pretty much straight down starting right before the bonds closed," he added.
March S&P 500s ultimately collapsed to 774.00, posting more than a 25-point range on the day.
"It was heavy profit-taking and then it was panic profit-taking and then everyone was just scrambling," one S&P 500 futures trader said.

He said sell stops at 795.00 yanked March to support at 791.50 to 792.00 where small dealer buying briefly stemmed the declines. But the bearish tide soon reappeared and March collapsed without a look back, he said.
"The Dow was down 50 before it even blinked," he said.
Traders called the sell-off a decisive rejection of the new record high, and some said declines to the mid-700.00 zone are now likely.

"This is a very significant outside day," said Jay Hohmann, futures trader for DLJ in New York. "This is very significant because this could be the point where the market returns back to the 760.00 level or so," he said.
Others pegged important support at the 50-day moving average of 756.25 and at 749.55, the quarter retracement of the six-month upmove.
Some programs were noted on the declines, traders said.
"It was panic, you can't blame it on programs," another S&P 500 trader said. "There are bears in the woods and a lot of technical selling," he added.
Nasdaq 100 futures also surged early into record territory, driven by the momentum of a recent series of all-time highs. But the technology index also fell apart late.
Some said the market had grown illiquid at these record levels in Nasdaq and S&Ps and was due for a correction.
"Overall this is not very bad because it will return us to levels where people feel a little more comfortable with the market," Hohmann said.
He noted ample support for March even if it drops as low as 740.00.
"The flight path has been corrected to a more reasonable level of attack," he added.
March S&Ps closed down 11.35 points at 780.25, KCBT Value Lines fell 5.30 to 702.50, NYSE Composites dropped 5.40 to 410.15, Nikkeis were down 410 at 17,735 and Nasdaq 100s were off 13.60 at 919.50.
